name: Welding Technology
description: Welding programmes teach people to join metal to a code standard — shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux-cored and gas tungsten arc welding, on plate and on pipe, in every position. ⚠ It is a test-based trade: what you can weld is decided by a test coupon, not by a transcript.
degreesNote: Florida teaches this as CLOCK-HOUR career certificates. The state framework **Welding Technology** runs **1,050 hours across three occupational completion points** — welder assistant, shielded metal arc welder, then welder — and each is a hireable exit on its own. An **Advanced Welding Technology** certificate (750 hours, two more completion points) adds pipe and career preparation. ⚠⚠ **Florida renumbered these courses in 2025 and BOTH families are still being taught**: the new staged sequence (PMT0070–0074) at 30 institutions and the older process-by-process one (PMT0011–0016 — SMAW, GMAW, FCAW, GTAW, pipe) at 19, with **16 colleges carrying both**. Register by the PROGRAMME, not the course number. ⚠ A few state colleges add an associate degree above the certificates, usually in welding or manufacturing technology.

cips.note: Welding technology/welder — the programme itself. **47 Florida public institutions** award in it and 1,082 credentials were awarded in 2023, which makes it one of the largest career certificates in the state. Most of those institutions are district technical colleges.

related.note: ⚠ Where the step up lives: manufacturing and engineering technology associate degrees take welders into inspection, fabrication supervision and quality — the usual route out of the booth without leaving the industry.

The other large clock-hour trade taught at the same technical colleges, and a common second choice for students deciding between the two. Both are test-and-certification trades; the difference is diagnosis versus fabrication.
